body:
## Summary

`/fix` had one mode. `--ci-cd` (issue #1733) points at a repository, collects its
real state from the GitHub API, writes a remediation issue from that state plus a
fixed standard prompt, and hands the issue to
`/solve --development-log --deep-analysis --auto-merge`.

Issue #2184 asks for the same machine aimed at a different target — update every
dependency, in every language — plus a `/solve` option, off by default, so the
same instructions can ride along with any other task.

```
/fix owner/repo --update-all-dependencies
/task owner/repo --update-all-dependencies          # generate the issue, stop there
/solve <issue-url> --update-all-dependencies        # attach it to unrelated work
/hive <repo-url>  --update-all-dependencies
```

Three things made this more than a copy of `--ci-cd`:

1. **The obvious update command is usually the wrong one.** `npm update` stays
   inside the existing semver ranges and never crosses a major.
   `cargo update --breaking` is nightly-only. Maven versions usually live in
   `<properties>`, not in `<dependency>`. A prompt that says "update all
   dependencies" without saying *how* produces a run that bumps patch versions
   and reports success. Every command shipped in the catalog is quoted from its
   own upstream documentation in
   [`data/ecosystem-update-commands.json`](docs/case-studies/issue-2184/data/ecosystem-update-commands.json).
2. **`/fix` was written for one mode.** Argument parsing, GitHub access and issue
   building all lived in `fix.ci-cd.lib.mjs`. Adding a second mode by copying it
   would have left two divergent copies of the `/solve` handoff.
3. **The prompt has two carriers.** The same paragraphs go into the generated
   issue body and into the AI system prompt. They are built from one tagged
   array, so the two cannot drift.

Fixes #2184

## What changed

**The new mode** (`src/fix.update-dependencies.lib.mjs`, `src/fix.update-dependencies-issue.lib.mjs`)

- A catalog of 15 ecosystems — JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Rust, Go, C#/.NET,
  Java/Kotlin/Scala, PHP, Ruby, Elixir/Erlang, Dart/Flutter, Swift, Haskell,
  GitHub Actions, Docker, infrastructure as code — each with its manifests,
  lockfiles, path patterns, Dependabot values, verified update command, and the
  trap that ecosystem hides.
- Detection unions **language** signals with **file-path** signals. It has to:
  GitHub's language stats for this repository name JavaScript, Shell, Dockerfile
  and Go Template — neither npm nor GitHub Actions — while the file tree holds
  `package.json`, five Dockerfiles and five workflows
  ([`repo-languages.json`](docs/case-studies/issue-2184/data/repo-languages.json),
  [`hive-mind-manifest-inventory.json`](docs/case-studies/issue-2184/data/hive-mind-manifest-inventory.json)).
- The generated issue leads with the ecosystem inventory and the standard prompt,
  ends with a ready `.github/dependabot.yml` — real YAML, one `updates:` entry per
  `package-ecosystem` value whose manifest is actually committed, with the
  directories it was found in (Renovate named as the alternative) — and keeps the
  collected evidence in a collapsed block so it stays available without
  displacing the instructions.
- Existing tools are configured, not reimplemented. What the prompt asks for is
  the part no bot does: read the migration guide, adapt the code, delete the
  hand-rolled implementation upstream now provides, bring a dependency pinned in
  four places to one version, and report a blocking upstream bug rather than
  silently pinning back.

**The `/solve` option** (`src/solve.config.lib.mjs`, `src/update-dependencies.prompts.lib.mjs`)

- One entry in `SOLVE_OPTION_DEFINITIONS`, so it reaches `/solve`, `/hive` and
  their Telegram commands through the existing passthrough derivation rather than
  by hand.
- The sub-prompt module follows the `architecture-care` / `handoff` pattern and is
  wired into all six tool prompt builders — claude, codex, opencode, agent, qwen,
  gemini. A test asserts all six, so a seventh tool added without the wiring fails.
- Paragraphs another enabled option already supplies (`--deep-analysis`,
  `--development-log`) are dropped instead of repeated, reusing the `providedBy`
  tagging from #1733. `KEEP_WORKING_PROMPT` is filtered out because `/solve`
  emits it itself.
- **Disabled by default** (`default: false`); the sub-prompt returns `''` unless
  the flag is on.

**Extraction, so the second mode did not fork the first** (`src/fix.args.lib.mjs`, `src/fix.github.lib.mjs`, `src/fix.mjs`)

- `fix.args.lib.mjs` — repository parsing, `partitionFixArgs`, and the `FIX_MODES`
  registry. `partitionFixArgs` returns `modes[]`, so "no mode" and "two modes" are
  both first-class errors instead of one mode silently winning.
- `fix.github.lib.mjs` — the shared GitHub reads, plus `getRepositoryFiles`, which
  reports GitHub's `truncated` flag rather than pretending a truncated tree is
  the whole repository.
- `fix.mjs` drives a mode table, so validate → prepare → dry-run → create → solve
  exists once. `fix.ci-cd.lib.mjs` re-exports the moved symbols; `--ci-cd`
  behaviour is unchanged.
- The Telegram `/fix` default implied `--ci-cd` unconditionally. On top of an
  explicit `--update-all-dependencies` that would make the CLI reject the request
  as two modes at once, so it now checks for *any* mode.

**Documentation**

`docs/DEPENDENCY-UPDATE-BEST-PRACTICES.md` is linked from every generated issue
and from the sub-prompt — and did not exist, so every generated issue carried a
404. It is now written in all four repository languages
([en](docs/DEPENDENCY-UPDATE-BEST-PRACTICES.md) ·
[zh](docs/DEPENDENCY-UPDATE-BEST-PRACTICES.zh.md) ·
[hi](docs/DEPENDENCY-UPDATE-BEST-PRACTICES.hi.md) ·
[ru](docs/DEPENDENCY-UPDATE-BEST-PRACTICES.ru.md)): what "all dependencies"
means, the per-ecosystem command table with its traps, ten principles, and how to
keep it current with Dependabot or Renovate. The `/fix` section of all four
READMEs and one row per language in `docs/CONFIGURATION*.md` document the mode
and the option where users look for them.

## Case study

[`docs/case-studies/issue-2184/`](docs/case-studies/issue-2184/README.md) —
requested explicitly by the issue. Nine evidence files in `data/`, the ten
requirements read out of the issue (its comment thread is empty, so the
description is the whole specification), what the three prior-art "update all
dependencies in all N languages" issues contributed, the survey of existing tools
and why they are recommended rather than reimplemented, and a per-requirement
solution plan including the options that were rejected.
[`research-sources.json`](docs/case-studies/issue-2184/research-sources.json)
records each source with the finding it settled.

**The research caught a defect in the code before release.** The catalog declared
`dependabot: ['npm', 'yarn', 'pnpm', 'bun']` for JavaScript, but `pnpm` is not one
of the 33 accepted `package-ecosystem` values — GitHub covers `pnpm-lock.yaml`
under `npm`. Since those values are printed verbatim into the recommended
`.github/dependabot.yml`, the generated issue would have advised a configuration
GitHub rejects. Fixed in 0e01a54c, with a regression test that checks every
catalog value against the captured reference list.

**Reading the dry run against that same list caught a second one.** The section
printed *every* `package-ecosystem` value of every detected ecosystem, so on this
repository it recommended `yarn` and `bun` (no `yarn.lock`, no `bun.lock`),
`devcontainers`, `terraform`, `opentofu`, `pre-commit` and `gitsubmodule` — twelve
values where five are true, and Dependabot reports a missing manifest on every run
for each of the wrong seven. The catalog now carries `dependabotEvidence`, the file
a value actually reads (`yarn` ⇢ `yarn.lock`, `helm` ⇢ `Chart.yaml`, `terraform` ⇢
`*.tf`), with a `dependabotFallback` for an ecosystem detected by language alone;
and the section renders the configuration itself rather than a list of names.
Running it here now produces exactly `npm`, `docker` (`/`, `/coolify`,
`/experiments/solve-dockerize`), `docker-compose`, `github-actions` and `helm`
(`/helm/hive-mind`).

## Tests

`tests/test-fix-update-dependencies.mjs` — 52 tests, in the default suite:

- catalog shape, uniqueness, immutability, and every Dependabot value against the
  33 GitHub accepts (the `pnpm` regression);
- the generated `dependabot.yml`: the three keys GitHub requires, evidence gating
  (`yarn` only with a `yarn.lock`, `terraform` and `opentofu` never together),
  `directory:` for one directory and `directories:` for several, `github-actions`
  at `/`, and the monorepo truncation cap;
- detection from languages, from file paths, and from a truncated tree;
- issue title and body, and the `providedBy` filtering in both carriers;
- `/fix` argument partitioning: mode required, exactly one mode, forwarding of
  everything `/fix` does not consume;
- the option reaching `/solve`, `/hive` passthrough, option-name suggestions, and
  all six tool prompts — and producing nothing when it is off;
- Telegram `/fix` defaults in both directions and the two `/task` generated-issue
  modes.

Running the mode against this repository caught a second defect before release:
two catalog entries are prose rather than a command ("bump every `uses:`
reference…", "bump each `FROM` base-image tag…") and the renderer wrapped every
update command in a code span. Markdown code spans do not nest, so those two
lines rendered with their middles as prose and their ends as code. They are now
marked `updateCommandIsProse` and rendered as-is, with a test that checks both
halves of the rule.


`tests/test-issue-2135-log-explosion.mjs` walks a list of files that spawn
children and asserts each names a signal rather than interpolating a null exit
code. `fix.ci-cd-issue.lib.mjs` was on that list; the extraction moved the spawner
to `fix.github.lib.mjs`, so the guard now follows it there.

## Verification

```
npm run format:check      # all matched files use Prettier code style
npm run lint              # clean
npm run check:duplication # 10.10% (threshold 11)
npm run check:secrets     # clean
scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh
node tests/docs-validation.mjs
node tests/test-docs-language-sync.mjs   # en / zh / hi / ru in sync
npm test
```

## Reproduction

```bash
# Preview the generated issue without creating anything:
./src/fix.mjs https://github.com/owner/repo --update-all-dependencies --dry-run

# Create the issue but do not start /solve:
./src/fix.mjs owner/repo --update-all-dependencies --no-solve

# Attach the same instructions to an unrelated task:
./src/solve.mjs https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/1 --update-all-dependencies
```
title: `/fix --update-all-dependencies`: update every dependency of every ecosystem, and the `/solve` option that carries it
